question.problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{4}{x}y=-6{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2},\,y(1)=\frac{1}{9},\,y>0.
$$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{2}{x}\,z=3{x}^{2}
$$

using the substitution $z={y}^{-1/2}.$*
question.worked_solution:
The substitution $z={y}^{-1/2}$ transforms the given equation into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{2}{x}\,z=3{x}^{2},
$$

with the initial condition

$$
z(1)={(\frac{1}{9})}^{-1/2}=3\,.
$$

The above equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x)
$$

with

$$
P(x)=-\frac{2}{x},\,Q(x)=3{x}^{2}\,.
$$

We then compute an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{-2\int 1/x\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}^{-2}} \\  & ={x}^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)={x}^{-2}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{2}{x}\,z) & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot 3{x}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\,z & =3 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,z) & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,z)\,\text{d}x & =\int 3\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,z & =3x+C \\ z & =3{x}^{3}+C{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we determine the value of $C$ that satisfies the initial condition $z(1)=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z(1) & =3 \\ 3(1)^{3}+C(1)^{2} & =3 \\ 3+C & =3 \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have 

$$
z=3{x}^{3}\,.
$$

Finally, we determine $y(x)$ by substituting the solution into $z={y}^{-1/2}.$ This results in

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{-1/2} & =z \\ {y}^{-1/2} & =3{x}^{3} \\ {y}^{1/2} & =\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}} \\ y & =\frac{1}{9{x}^{6}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
